subject: Banking
title: Bernie Madoff's Bank Enablers
description: A micro-lesson that makes Bernie Madoff's Bank Enablers usable.

hook.text: Bernie Madoff ran a $65 billion Ponzi scheme for decades.

buildup.text: Madoff's returns were impossibly consistent: 10-12% every year regardless of market conditions.

discovery.text: JPMorgan filed a suspicious activity report with UK authorities but not with US regulators.

twist.text: JPMorgan paid $2.6 billion for failing to report suspicious activity.

climax.text: Banks are supposed to be the first line of defense against fraud.

punchline.text: $65 billion Ponzi. Banks saw red flags. They chose fees over reporting.

quiz.question: Why didn't JPMorgan report Madoff to US authorities?
options: They suspected fraud but profited from the banking relationship
